title: delivered_amount, faucet funding and Testnet endpoint history
abstract: Operational lessons on faucet wallets, partial payments, validated settlement and historical transaction availability.
tags: faucet funding and Testnet endpoint history
body:
For XRP Payment settlement, delivered_amount is evidence of what the destination actually received. Checking the requested Amount alone can accept an underpayment when partial-payment semantics apply. Our checks bind destination, currency, amount and invoice identity to the intended purchase. Escrow settlement has its own validation and object checks. Issued-token escrow additionally requires the exact RippleState balance delta, with the correct currency, issuer and sign. A requested amount is never sufficient proof of delivery.

Original wording below is historical, including any relative freshness wording. #342 diagnostics distinguish the observed 606-second host sleep from inferred runtime risk; see evidence/soak-nov4.md. It is not a new ledger incident.

A living record for the SFF judges. 35 catalogued items plus dated tooling incidents: 16 implementation findings and 4 live escrow spike findings below, plus the 15 September research submissions in the appendix. The original source and history audit was recorded on 2 Nov 2026; dated additions below identify live-network observations separately. The original log dates are audit dates; the evidence column dates the original work. The four B17–B20 entries are fresh Testnet observations from 3 Nov 2026. The eight writers and their content are synthetic. Offline settlement is SIMULATED; historical live receipts are XRPL TESTNET · no real value. Neither is evidence of mainnet readiness.

The first SDK-lane npm ci failed with ENOTEMPTY while removing an Electron transitive dependency; a retry completed without dependency changes. Evidence: SDK v1 lane check output and scripts/check-sdk-package.mjs for the subsequent clean tarball check. Workaround: retry installation. Suggested fix: make npm ci cleanup tolerate transient nonempty dependency directories. Severity: low; mainnet impact: none observed. This was local npm tooling, not XRPL or x402.

The #278 UC3 runner created its first run using Store's default SIMULATED label while injecting a real Testnet payer; the gate audit refused the inconsistent snapshot (missing_rail_label). Evidence: docs/evidence/verify-278.md and verify-278/summary.json. Workaround: pass the explicit Testnet mode labels, correct the harness metadata and re-export/re-check the same durable run; no replacement payment. Suggested fix: require explicit rail labels in standalone Testnet harness constructors. Severity: low (local evidence tooling). Mainnet impact: none observed; no value funds. This was not a ledger or x402 failure.

Local scorecard evaluation at 5953559: an initial attempt hit OpenAI Decisions HTTP 503 ("Decision inference is unavailable") on one coverage request and correctly refused to publish a baseline. Evidence: eval/scorecard/out/2026-11-02T16-27-35.998Z-live/requests.jsonl and cost.json (local ignored artifacts; US$0.1233354 including all calls). Workaround: one bounded transient retry, with both attempts cached/metered; the next complete run published the pre-menu baseline in eval/scorecard/history.jsonl. Suggested tooling fix: retain per-phase progress and retry transient inference errors without discarding successful calls. Severity: low for local evaluation; mainnet impact: none observed (all settlement SIMULATED). This was a model/tooling incident, not an XRPL, x402, Starter Kit or Testnet failure. Signing the menu with existing XRPL keys required no new wallet/API operation; no signing friction was observed. The local .env key also needs an explicit evaluation mapping; make scorecard LIVE=1 now handles that without loading wallet seeds.
